answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The yarrow multiplier is published, charged in marble, and saffron lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3289 identities would post 1162 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
